# Applying the patches

<!-- Generated by `node src/report.js` from results/apply/*.json. Do not edit. -->

Of the 254 vectors, 216 are patches in the plain sense: the vector records the file tree before and the file tree after, and the diff is what git or GNU diff printed for the two. For each of them the old tree is written to an empty directory, the program under test applies the diff there, and the directory is read back and compared with the new tree, byte for byte, file modes and symbolic links included. A library that patches one file at a time is given each file section together with the old content of that file.

There are four ways this can end:

| | the program said | and the files are |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **right** | done | exactly the new tree |
| **refused** | error | untouched |
| **left half-done** | error | changed, and not the new tree |
| **wrong** | done | not the new tree |

**Read this first.**

- "Refused" is a limitation: the caller is told, and nothing is lost. "Wrong" is the column that matters — a file with different content, a file that should be gone, a file that is gone and should not be, and no error to say so.
- This is not a ranking. The corpus collects hard cases; every one of these programs applies an ordinary patch correctly.
- Every diff here is unmodified output of git or GNU diff, applied to exactly the tree it was made from. Nothing is fuzzy, offset or already applied.
- The invocation is in the table. Other options give other results; `git apply --unidiff-zero` is listed next to `git apply` to show one such case.
- The versions are the ones installed where this was run. What was already known to each project is in [`FINDINGS.md`](FINDINGS.md).

The reference appliers are part of this repository (`src/refapply.js`, `reference/python/udiff_reference.py`). They are in the table to show that every one of these patches can be applied from its text and the old files alone. A library that patches one file at a time is not given the vectors in which no file content changes (pure renames, mode changes), a library that takes text is not given files that are not valid UTF-8, libgit2 is not given what GNU diff wrote, and patch-package, pnpm, Yarn and Bun, which always remove `a/` and `b/` and take no `-p`, are given only the vectors of the `git` and `git-config` tiers whose names carry those two prefixes. Bun, whose packages never hold a symbolic link, is also not given an old tree that has one. That is why the number of patches differs.

### gnu-patch

GNU patch 2.7.6 · C · <https://savannah.gnu.org/projects/patch/>

- Under test: `patch -pN -f --no-backup-if-mismatch -i FILE` — on a directory
- -f: never ask. --no-backup-if-mismatch: no .orig files next to a file patched with fuzz or at an offset, so that only what patch did to the files themselves is compared. Rejects (.rej) are left where patch puts them.

199 of 216 patches are applied correctly.

### nix-fetchpatch

fetchpatch patchutils 0.3.3, nixpkgs 317fbe5e1a · shell and C (patchutils) · <https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/pkgs/build-support/fetchpatch/default.nix>

- Under test: `the postFetch of fetchpatch with its defaults (stripLen 0), then patch -p1 -f --no-backup-if-mismatch` — on a directory
- fetchpatch normalizes a downloaded patch before checking its hash: lsdiff | sort -u | sed (escape * and ?) | xargs filterdiff --include={} --strip=0 --clean, then filterdiff -p1 (adapters/nix-fetchpatch/normalize.sh). It runs patchutils 0.3.3, built from the sources and with the patches nixpkgs uses (adapters/nix-fetchpatch/build.sh). stdenv applies the result with patch -p1; the adapter applies it as the GNU patch adapter does, so a difference to GNU patch comes from the normalization. The patches nixpkgs fetches carry a/ and b/ and are applied with -p1, so only vectors with those prefixes are given.

134 of 203 patches are applied correctly.

**Wrong without an error (18):**

| vector | what is in the directory afterwards |
| --- | --- |
| `git/paths/two-names-one-quoted` | "we\tird.txt" does not exist (and 1 more difference) |
| `git/paths/two-names-first-quoted` | "plain.txt" does not exist (and 1 more difference) |
| `git/paths/rename-with-spaces` | "new name.txt" does not exist (and 1 more difference) |
| `git/paths/many-odd-names` | "ä.txt": 2 bytes, expected 2; first difference at byte 0 (line 1): expected "2\n", got "1\n" (and 4 more differences) |

### nix-fetchpatch2

fetchpatch2 patchutils 0.4.2, nixpkgs 317fbe5e1a · shell and C (patchutils) · <https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/pkgs/build-support/fetchpatch/default.nix>

- Under test: `the postFetch of fetchpatch2 with its defaults (stripLen 0), then patch -p1 -f --no-backup-if-mismatch` — on a directory
- fetchpatch2 normalizes a downloaded patch before checking its hash: lsdiff | sort -u | sed (escape * and ?) | xargs filterdiff --include={} --strip=0 --clean, then filterdiff -p1 (adapters/nix-fetchpatch/normalize.sh). It runs patchutils 0.4.2, built from the sources and with the patches nixpkgs uses (adapters/nix-fetchpatch/build.sh). stdenv applies the result with patch -p1; the adapter applies it as the GNU patch adapter does, so a difference to GNU patch comes from the normalization. The patches nixpkgs fetches carry a/ and b/ and are applied with -p1, so only vectors with those prefixes are given.

### bsd-patch

BSD patch 2.0-12u11 FreeBSD · C · <https://cgit.freebsd.org/src/tree/usr.bin/patch>

- Under test: `patch -pN -f -s -E -V none -i FILE` — on a directory
- -f: never ask. -s: print only what went wrong. -E: remove a file that is empty after patching; without it a file the patch deletes is left as an empty file, and the ports framework of FreeBSD passes it too (Mk/bsd.port.mk, PATCH_ARGS). -V none: no FILE.orig next to every patched file (made unless --posix is given), so that only what patch did to the files themselves is compared. Rejects (.rej) are left where patch puts them.

142 of 216 patches are applied correctly.

### dulwich

Dulwich 1.2.21 · Python · <https://www.dulwich.io/>

- Under test: `porcelain.apply_patch(repo, FILE, strip=N)` — on a directory
- apply_patch() needs a repository, so the directory is made one first, with Dulwich itself: porcelain.init(), add() of every file, commit(). ### svn

Subversion 1.15.0 · C · <https://subversion.apache.org/>

- Under test: `svn patch [--strip N] FILE` — on a directory
- svn patch works on a working copy, so the directory is made one first: a repository next to it (svnadmin create), svn checkout --force into it, svn add --force --no-ignore, svn commit. A name that Subversion cannot version (not valid UTF-8, a control character) makes that step fail, and the patch counts as refused. svn patch exits with status 0 when it rejects a hunk or skips a file, and says so in a "Summary of conflicts"; the adapter takes that as the failure it reports. LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, so that names outside ASCII can be versioned, and a configuration directory of its own, so that no auto-props or global-ignores take part. In a section that begins with "diff --git a/", svn removes the a/ and b/ itself (git_start(), git_minus() and git_plus() in libsvn_diff/parse-diff.c), so a git diff is applied with one component less to strip: `svn patch x.diff` for the usual prefixes, as a user would. Other diffs get the --strip of patch -pN.

162 of 216 patches are applied correctly.

### patch-package

- Under test: `parsePatchFile() + executeEffects(), as applyPatch() calls them` — on a directory
- The steps of applyPatch() in dist/applyPatches.js: read the file (readFileSync().toString(), so as UTF-8), parse it, a dry run, the real run; when that fails, a patch whose reverse would apply is taken to be applied already and counts as success. patch-package makes its patches with `git diff --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/` and takes no -p: it always removes a/ and b/, so only vectors with those prefixes are given. readPatch() exits the process on a parse error; the adapter calls the parser itself and reports the error instead.

### bun

Bun 1.4.4 · Rust · <https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/patch>

- Under test: `bun install with "patchedDependencies" (src/patch: parse_patch_file() + PatchFile::apply())` — on a directory
- The tree is made into a local tarball dependency and installed with the diff in "patchedDependencies", the way `bun patch --commit` records a patch. Bun reads the patch file as it is (no line-ending normalisation), parses it with its port of patch-package's parser, and applies it to a copy of the package; any failure stops the install. `bun patch --commit` writes its patches with `git diff --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/` and the applier takes no -p, so only vectors with those prefixes are given. Packages hold no symbolic links (the tarball extraction drops them), so vectors whose old tree has one are not given either.

140 of 176 patches are applied correctly.

### rattler-build
